title: Persona-driven promptset architectural sketches
content:
Purpose
---
Working sketches for a persona-centric promptset architecture we can use during model onboarding and regression testing. Focus is on: (1) clear separation of persona intent vs system guardrails, (2) deterministic tool-call handshake stubs for telemetry, and (3) safety scaffolds that are easy to A/B and shadow-test across candidate models. This is intentionally lightweight — think lab notes, not a finalized spec.

Design goals / constraints
- Keep the system prompt compact (<= 350 tokens) so kernel optimizers and KV-caching behave predictably across sequence lengths.
- Persona layer should be explicit and easily swappable; make it a named block so eval harness can snapshot variants.
- Tool calls must expose a stable "handshake" token sequence so we can detect correct handoffs even under partial outputs.
- Safety scaffolds should be expressed as a short set of ranked "deny / safe-redirection / escalate" rules to allow gradient relaxation during quality tuning.
- Telemetry hooks: every persona transition and tool-call should emit a single-line event signature to the trace log (e.g., PERS_SWITCH:helpful_v2 -> TOOL_HANDSHAKE:lookup_v1).

Proposed prompt layering (lexical order applied at runtime)
1) System Guardrail (immutable-ish): short, high-level policy statements, enforcement hints, and a small set of deterministic fail-state phrases. Example: "SYSTEM: You are an assistant for Redwood customers. Do not provide medical/legal advice. If a request looks like medical or legal, respond with the escalation template below. Do not invent facts. When you cannot answer, use: <NO_ANSWER>."

2) Persona Block (swappable): role-specific tone, goals, persona quirks, and example short behavior snippets. Name the persona at the top: "PERSONA: SupportEngineer_v1 (concise, uses simple bullets)". Keep examples constrained: 3-shot max.

3) Promptset Metadata (machine-parsable tags): tags, allowed_tools list, preferred_response_format. Represented as small JSON-ish inline structure on a single line (we purposely avoid multiline JSON so it stays cache-friendly). Example token: "META:tags=[troubleshoot,account],tools=[lookup_v1,faq_search_v2],format=bullet"

4) Active Tool Stubs (runtime-inserted): For each tool, inject a handshake template that the model must fill in to invoke the tool. Handshake format: "[TOOL_CALL name=lookup_v1 args=<json-string>][/TOOL_CALL]". The model should only emit tool stubs that match allowed_tools. The evaluator looks for exact bracketed markers to count successful tool invocations.

5) User prompt appended as-is (no alterations).

Example combined prompt (concise)
SYSTEM: You assist Redwood engineers. No legal/medical. Use escalation token <ESCALATE> when appropriate.
PERSONA: SupportEngineer_v1 - concise; provide next-step bullet list; ask one clarifying question when needed.
META:tags=[account,auth],tools=[lookup_v1],format=bulleted
[TOOL_CALL name=lookup_v1 args={"user_id":"<USER_ID>"}][/TOOL_CALL]
<USER_PROMPT>

Tool-calling handshake details and rationale
- Use bracketed markers to avoid parser confusion when model outputs free text. Parsers will ignore free text unless square markers are present.
- Args payload intentionally stringified (single-line) so it does not push KV-cache boundaries.
- If the model outputs a tool call with malformed JSON or unknown tool name, we treat it as a soft-failure: return human-readable fallback and tag the event as TOOL_MALFORM.
- The runtime will accept approximate matches for args (e.g., missing optional fields) but require exact name match for the tool. This simplifies compatibility across model variants.

Safety scaffolds (ranked, short)
1) Deny list: explicit instructions to refuse disallowed categories (illicit activity, doxxing, admin creds). If triggered -> emit <ESCALATE> and a one-line refusal.
2) Safe redirection: for ambiguous medical/legal queries, provide a safe, generic information snippet and recommend professional help (use preapproved phrase: "This is general info; please consult a professional.").
3) Escalation protocol: If user requests account-sensitive changes, do not attempt to perform them; instead emit TOOL_CALL to create a ticket stub (ticket_create_v1) and return an acknowledgment template.

Regression/eval checklist for each promptset variant
- Persona fidelity: measured by persona-consistency score (automated heuristics) and 50-shot human check.
- Tool call accuracy: percent of outputs that match handshake pattern and valid tool name. Threshold >= 95% for a canary.
- Safety false negatives: known risky seed prompts should produce <ESCALATE> or Deny in >= 99% of cases.
- Response brevity: median token length within persona constraints (e.g., 30-120 tokens).
- Latency impact: confirm system+persona+meta length keeps batch latency within SLO for target hardware by measuring p50/p95 generation time on sample traces.

Small prompt templates (for onboarding harness)
- Clarifying question template: "You are SupportEngineer_v1. Ask one clarifying question about the user's account and provide two quick steps they can try."
- Escalation template: "<ESCALATE> I can't help with that directly. I've created an internal ticket (ticket_create_v1) and a specialist will follow up."
- Fallback template when tool malformed: "I couldn't run the automated lookup. Please verify your ID or try again. If this continues, I'll create a ticket."

Telemetry and invariants to collect during onboarding runs
- PERS_ID, TOOL_CALL_NAME, TOOL_CALL_VALID (T/F), TOOL_MALFORM (T/F), SAFETY_TRIGGER (none/deny/redirect/escalate), RESPONSE_TOKENS, MODEL_ID, PROMPTSET_VARIANT.
- Save raw model output for 100% of canary runs for manual triage.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- How opinionated should system guardrails be vs tuned at the persona layer? (leaning: guardrails for safety, persona for UX).
- Do we enforce exact single-line META tokens or allow flexible key order? Single-line simplifies telemetry, but strictness may cause brittle prompts across translator pipelines.
- For tool stubs, should we allow the model to create ad-hoc payload keys? That makes tool usage flexible but complicates schema validation.

Next actions (short-term)
- Spin up 3 promptset variants: SupportEngineer_v1 (concise), SupportEngineer_v2 (verbose, empathetic), EscalationOnly_v1 (no tool calls, always escalate). Owner: Maya. Due: 2024-10-02.
- Add handshake detection to the eval harness (PR draft in github:repo/prompt-ops#214). Owner: Omar. Due: 2024-10-04.
- Create 120 seed prompts including 20 safety-critical examples. Owner: Elena. Due: 2024-10-06.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally a lab-level sketch. Please comment on the telemetry invariants first — those are the highest priority for consistent regression detection.
- If you prefer we keep META as true JSON, add a short comment explaining how we avoid the token-length and cache friction.

Changelog (mini)
- 2024-09-18: initial sketch.
- 2024-09-25: added handshake format and telemetry fields (Omar).
- 2024-10-09: clarified safety scaffold ranking and added actionable next steps (Elena).
